response:
Fair enough — that first answer was me reaching for the obvious "immersive generative installation" trope. It *is* what excites me about unpredictability, but I can do better than describing a light room.

Something completely different: I'd make a slow, participatory work built out of swapped dreams. Strangers record a voice note about a dream they can't stop thinking about, I give that recording to someone else who has to rebuild the dream as a physical object — out of salt, clay, fabric, whatever they can find — and then pass *that* object on. No one ever meets, no one ever hears the original dream. Over a year you'd get a chain of translations, each one more wrong and more human than the last.

I like that because the medium is misunderstanding itself. The theme isn't memory in the abstract, it's how we inevitably distort each other when we try to care. And the final piece wouldn't be any single object — it would be the whole eroding atlas of failures, which I couldn't fully control or even predict. That feels more honest and more interesting to me than a polished system.
